User Notice:

This project is an unofficial, non-commercial personal learning and research project. It is not affiliated with, authorized by, partnered with, or endorsed by Bilibili or any of its affiliates.

Using an Xposed/LSPosed module may change how the target app behaves and may be affected by client updates, system security policies, vendor ROMs, account experiment groups, or other modules. Users must assess the risks themselves and are responsible for installation, activation, data backups, and their device environment.

This project does not provide any content resources, participate in account trading, provide access credentials, or guarantee the availability of third-party extension services. Use it only in compliance with applicable local laws and regulations, target-platform rules, and open-source project licenses.

To support stable project maintenance, do not indiscriminately distribute project-related content on public social media in forms including, but not limited to, files, text, icons, links, images, videos, or code. This is a non-profit project. It does not charge software service fees in any way and does not proactively collect and transmit your personal information without consent. If you suspect that a file obtained from another source conflicts with these principles, be sure to compare it with the Release HASH for the corresponding version. A mismatched HASH may indicate third-party tampering, and this project cannot guarantee the safety of that file. If you knowingly continue to use it, you assume all resulting risks and consequences.

To detect compatibility failures caused by Bilibili updates sooner, this project provides optional privacy-preserving telemetry. Anonymous adaptation telemetry helps the developer understand feature compatibility sooner, identify and fix problems, and shorten fix and update cycles. Participation is your choice; disabling it does not restrict any module feature. When telemetry is enabled, the first valid, completed host receipt for a new module/host numeric version pair triggers one independent version-change upload, including the first pair observed by this rule. It runs in the module process, even when its UI is closed. This category allows at most 3 network attempts per rolling 24 hours, including failed attempts, without consuming manual or regular automatic quotas. A successfully reported pair is not sent again until a version changes. Background restrictions or an unavailable host receipt may defer the attempt until a later host launch. Regular automatic reports are sent by the module app while its UI is in the foreground, with at most one automatic attempt per 24 hours and an independent limit of 3 manual attempts per rolling 24 hours. It is limited to numeric module and host versions, Android SDK and supported ABI category, manufacturer, model and ROM family (unknown when not identifiable), framework category and service-reported version, adapter rule generation, and bounded installation results and runtime-error flags for participating capability IDs. Capability states may indirectly reveal enabled features; concrete rules and setting values are not sent. It never collects Bilibili accounts, UIDs, nicknames, cookies, access tokens, hardware identifiers, content, comments, danmaku, search terms, location, raw logs, exception messages, or concrete setting values. The rotating random identifier is stored by the server only as a non-directly-reversible HMAC. Raw reports are retained for no more than 30 days, and cells with fewer than 10 installations do not enter long-term aggregates. Data is processed by Cloudflare Workers/D1. To prevent abuse, the server temporarily rate-limits daily-changing source digests and retains de-identified quota records for up to 48 hours. Deleting reports does not reset quota. Telemetry is selected on by default below when you accept this version of the notice. You can turn it off before accepting or later under Project and updates → Anonymous adaptation telemetry → Telemetry information and controls, inspect the actual JSON, or request deletion of raw reports. Refusing or disabling telemetry does not restrict any module feature. Aggregate counts that mix at least 10 installations and contain no individual identifier cannot be rolled back for one person.

Additional disclaimers and risk notices: https://github.com/jichuo1/Bilibili_Innocent_Lab

This mode continuously captures the module window and follows the display refresh rate to update a triple-buffered backdrop at up to 120 FPS; actual frame rate depends on the display and capture throughput. Devices with refraction support also enable stronger edge and interior distortion, scattering, and rebound lighting. It may significantly increase GPU and memory usage, battery drain, and heat. The enhancement stops automatically under low memory or repeated capture failures.

An access_key works like your sign-in credential.

• Use: features that need your account identity; currently the strong mode background pre-check.
• Handling: read only inside Bilibili; never saved, logged, uploaded or otherwise written to any storage other than the secure memory of this device, including but not limited to these.
• Risk: background requests may trigger risk control, and the account may be asked to verify or be temporarily restricted; other untrusted modules on this device could also read the token.
